description:
Execution boundary: planning approved; this issue does not authorize commits, pushes, merges, upstream publication, GitHub comments, live WhatsApp access, or real messages. Revalidate current source/Git state before implementation. Preserve unrelated work, including the already-edited docs/architecture.md. Track this work in the ZAQ Beadwork store even when files belong to the sibling package; do not initialize another store.
Read AGENTS.md in the affected repository. For ZAQ read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md plus the domain policies listed below. Read module documentation before editing. Source navigation uses Serena with bounded fallback if unavailable. Record test results honestly; plan approval is not completed-feature UX approval. Follow repository validation owners; no assertion weakening or unrelated refactors. Existing test changes outside the specifically approved contracts need human approval.

Required domain policies: DESIGN.md and docs/bo-components.md before UI edits; docs/phoenix.md; docs/testing-approach.md deterministic process tests. No visual redesign.

Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add:
ZAQ owners: lib/zaq_web/live/device_sign_in_polling.ex and lib/zaq_web/live/bo/communication/linked_device_ui.ex; minimal ChannelsLive.handle_info change. Extract a small generic local timer core under ZaqWeb.Live or extend the existing helper with generic primitives. Keep DeviceSignInPolling.schedule/3 and consume/3 compatibility wrapper so SystemConfigLive and People.CredentialsLive keep current interfaces and behavior. Do not move OAuth active-state logic into pairing.
Core handles schedule/cancel/consume using observation identity, interval and caller's active-state decision. Retain one live timer per observation, fresh token per tick, reject duplicates/queued stale messages. Keep pairing modal/async-result generation distinct from per-tick token: modal identity protects async responses, tick identity protects consumption. Do not rotate modal generation for each timer tick or accept expired/cancelled-session results. Identity must distinguish reopen/retry of the same config, not config ID alone.
Preserve OAuth 1000ms interval; linked-device 2000ms and current max-90-result observation bound/reset-on-open-or-retry (do not silently convert to a new wall-clock timeout). Preserve existing watching status decisions and provisional cancel/stale-session cleanup. Pairing requests, sessions, async results, attempts and presentation remain LinkedDeviceUI-owned. No backend/persistence/permission change and no timing retune.
APPROVAL: user confirmed point 5 clear in the same conversation as point 4. This approves reuse/refactoring, not changed intervals, retry semantics or weaker tests. Mechanical assertion plumbing changes must preserve tested scenario/intent; seek approval for any newly discovered behavioral expectation change.

Tests to add before implementation:
Extend test/zaq_web/live/device_sign_in_polling_test.exs and linked_device_ui_test.exs: one timer after repeat schedule, switch/reopen/retry identity fencing, duplicate tick rejection, consumed tick exactly one successor, queued tick after cancel, stale async result after close/switch, active/terminal states, 1000/2000 interval contract, 90 bound, session preserved on retry, stale provisional session discarded. Preserve existing property test for arbitrary schedule sequences and add pairing identity sequence coverage. Run relevant SystemConfigLive and People.CredentialsLive regressions. New browser E2E deferred to existing gate.

Branches/paths validated:
Open/reopen/switch/retry/close, active/terminal, duplicated/stale tick, stale/current async result, separate observation identities, all existing helper consumers.

Mocking plan:
Test real Process timers with explicit cleanup and injected/manual message delivery; no sleep-based timing assertions or global clock overrides. Use existing external dispatch fixtures for pairing requests; keep local timer logic real.

Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content:
Generic helper and wrapper @moduledoc/@doc explain separate identities and lifecycle. Update docs/services/channels.md only if clarification needed; no new independent polling policy document.

Action reuse assessment:
Decision: extend/extract local timer core from DeviceSignInPolling, reuse in LinkedDeviceUI. Existing helper hardcodes OAuth attempt shape, active-state component predicate and 1000ms; direct unchanged reuse is unsuitable. Pairing already duplicates cancel/send_after/generation behavior. Timer lifecycle is socket-local implementation detail with no standalone service Action or tool/workflow use. Inputs identity/interval/active decision -> socket/tick or stale; side effect one process timer. Verify unchanged consumers and sequence properties.

comments.text: Implemented shared local ObservationPolling schedule/cancel/consume core; DeviceSignInPolling retains public wrapper. LinkedDeviceUI keeps modal/async generation while each tick gets its own consumable token. OAuth 1000ms and pairing 2000ms/90-result limit retained; private metadata and timer assign preserve lifecycle cleanup. Red generic-core regression observed, green focused helper/UI suite: 13 tests + 1 property. Existing device credentials (BO AI/People) and WhatsApp onboarding consumer suites: 31 tests pass. Existing onboarding trace assertion mechanically updated from two-field to three-field timer envelope; same scenario/assertion intent, no UI expectation weakened. mix q passes; no visual/E2E authoring changes.
